title: Private: generate least-privilege IAM/KMS policies + document required key policy statements
author: Bruno Silva
description: Context: As part of KMS integration hardening + rotation work, we need Terraform outputs that (a) avoid overly broad KMS permissions by default and (b) clearly document which key policy statements customers must add for customer-managed keys (esp. Private). This PR updates our Private deployment modules to generate least-privilege IAM policies for KMS usage, makes the required KMS permissions explicit per component (control-plane vs data-plane), and adds documentation that customers can copy/paste into their CMK key policy (AWS KMS) / IAM bindings (GCP KMS) / access policies (Azure Key Vault, where applicable). Summary of changes: 1) Split KMS permissions by purpose: encrypt/decrypt vs describe/list vs grant management; 2) Default to resource-scoped permissions (key ARN) instead of wildcard; 3) Add optional "grant" support gated behind a new variable (kms_allow_grants=false by default) to support some Private installations that rely on grants for node identity patterns; 4) Introduce separate IAM policies for "runtime" (hot path) and "operator" (rotation/maintenance) so we can keep the runtime role minimal; 5) Update module inputs to accept kms_key_arn(s) and optionally kms_key_alias_arn, and validate that both aren’t set in unsafe combinations; 6) Docs: add a dedicated page describing the minimum required KMS key policy statements for customer-managed keys, including common pitfalls (missing kms:ViaService, missing principal ARN, wrong region, and IAM propagation delay notes). Backwards compatibility: Existing installations that used the prior broad policy will continue to work, but will see a planned diff (policy document changes). No changes to stateful resources other than IAM policy documents/attachments. For customers who currently rely on wildcard key permissions (rare), there is a temporary escape hatch variable kms_key_arn="*" which preserves old behavior, but it is marked deprecated and will be removed in a later major module version. Testing: terraform fmt/validate, tflint, and a plan/apply in a staging AWS account using a customer-managed CMK; verified that data-plane can decrypt sealed secrets and control-plane can perform rotation preflight checks. Also validated failure mode from SUP-18441 (AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt due to missing key policy statement) is addressed by the new docs + example key policy block. Rollout: recommend using this module version for new Private installs immediately; for upgrades, apply during a maintenance window if you’re also tightening key policies (IAM changes are typically non-disruptive, but key policy edits can break decrypt if done incorrectly).
commits: modules/private: split IAM policy docs into runtime vs operator roles
modules/private: scope KMS actions to provided key ARN and add variable validation
docs: add customer-managed KMS key policy requirements + troubleshooting section
examples/private: update sample usage to pass kms_key_arn and show optional grants flag
notable_snippets: AWS runtime policy now defaults to: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey on Resource = var.kms_key_arn (no kms:*).
Operator policy includes (optional) kms:CreateGrant/kms:ListGrants/kms:RevokeGrant behind var.kms_allow_grants, plus kms:GetKeyPolicy for validation workflows.

Docs include an example key policy statement granting the runtime role principal access to kms:Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey, and a separate statement granting the operator role grant management (if enabled).

Marcus Lin: The key policy example should emphasize that IAM policy alone is not enough for CMKs; need key policy principal allow + (recommended) explicit deny protection for everyone else. Also please include a note about kms:ViaService only if customers want to restrict to a service (e.g., EBS) — for our use we should not require it. Bruno Silva: Updated docs: added a "Key policy is authoritative" callout, included minimal allow statements for runtime/operator roles, and added an optional hardening section with kms:ViaService guidance marked as optional. Jordan Lee: Variable validation: if kms_key_alias_arn is provided, can we ensure it resolves to same region as the cluster? Otherwise we’ll keep getting confusing AccessDenied/NotFound. release_notes: Terraform Private modules now generate least-privilege KMS/IAM policies by default and include new documentation for required customer-managed KMS key policy statements. Upgrades may show IAM policy diffs; review and apply alongside any KMS key policy tightening.
